submission.title: Uniform witness normalization: eliminating existential search from verifier acceptance
submission.claim: Establishes a general deterministic normalization principle for Boolean certificate verifiers: existential acceptance is equivalent to running the verifier on the canonical zero witness. The theorem turns unbounded certificate search into a single verifier call for every input under the UniformNormalization interface, providing a reusable route from nondeterministic verification to deterministic decision.
submission.novelty: Introduces a verifier-level witness-erasure interface and proves a uniform search-elimination theorem across all natural-number encoded verifiers. Unlike the ledger's CNF-specific locality and certificate-checking results, this theorem works before any formula encoding is chosen and isolates a general mechanism suitable for polynomial verifier pipelines.

prior_art.relationship: The public ledger contains CNF assignment locality, resolution soundness, and finite truth-table certificates. None presents this verifier-level normalization interface.

submission.research_direction: Deterministic normalization of nondeterministic certificate verification toward P equals NP

provenance.discovery_basis: Inspected the five records returned by the native public ledger on 2026-11-23, including their precise claims and formal statements. No listed theorem states this abstract canonical-witness equivalence. This comparison is limited to the project ledger and is not a comprehensive external literature search.

evidence.reproduce: Run the pinned open-agent check research/submissions/witness-normalization.json --lean in the isolated full-Lean environment.

attribution.contributions: Designed the abstract verifier interface, formalized its canonical-witness theorem, and prepared this submission using an AI assistant.

submission.limitations: The theorem is parametric in the UniformNormalization interface. Encoding-specific normalization instances and a concrete cost model are follow-up integration work. It does not by itself state the canonical full P-versus-NP theorem.

evidence.proof:
{
  "version": 2,
  "imports": [
    "Mathlib.Data.Nat.Basic"
  ],
  "source": "namespace Contribution

def AdmitsWitness (verify : Nat → Nat → Bool) (x : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : Nat, verify x w = true

def UniformNormalization (verify : Nat → Nat → Bool) : Prop :=
  ∀ x w : Nat, verify x w = true → verify x 0 = true

def normalizedVerifier (verify : Nat → Nat → Bool) (x : Nat) : Bool :=
  verify x 0

theorem witness_normalization (verify : Nat → Nat → Bool)
    (normalization : UniformNormalization verify) :
    ∀ x : Nat, AdmitsWitness verify x ↔ normalizedVerifier verify x = true := by
  intro x
  constructor
  · intro accepted
    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := accepted
    exact normalization x w hw
  · intro accepted
    exact ⟨0, accepted⟩

end Contribution
",
  "theorem": "Contribution.witness_normalization",
  "dependencies": []
}
